input.quote: 11.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years. Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 11 creates a five-year committed term with automatic one-year renewals, and the only termination triggers in Section 11.2 are uncured material breach and insolvency. The 30-day notice in Section 11.1 is a non-renewal mechanic exercisable only at the end of a term, not a convenience exit. Corio therefore has no right to terminate for convenience at any point during a multi-year term, which the playbook treats as walk-away territory and a material failure of the fallback (which requires at least a 60-90 day customer convenience right). Commerce One likewise holds no convenience right, so no vendor-side exit needs deleting, and Sections 4 and 17 contain no early-termination fee or fee-acceleration mechanic. Redline inserts a new Section 11.3 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with refund of prepaid fees and confirms Commerce One has no mid-term convenience exit; the 60-90 day fallback is offered in the comment.

ops.text: 11.3 Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, without penalty or early termination charge, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio any prepaid fees allocable to the period after the effective date of such termination. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement runs an initial five (5) year term but gives us no exit other than for breach or insolvency, so we have added a convenience termination right on thirty (30) days' notice with a refund of prepaid fees, consistent with our playbook position. If a longer runway is needed we can move to 60-90 days' notice.
proposal.summary: Add Corio right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; no Commerce One convenience right mid-term.
